text:
noah: Hi all, just unboxed my MacBook Air (M1, macOS 14.0). Followed the setup flow and installed the profile but Okta keeps saying 'Device not trusted' when I try to sign in to Google Workspace. Any tips?

it-support: Welcome @noah! Quick Qs: did the device show as 'Enrolled' in System Settings > Profiles? Also can you paste the exact Okta error?

noah: In Profiles it shows 'Redwood MDM: Enrolled'. Okta error popup: 'This device does not meet device trust requirements. Please contact your IT administrator.' Screenshot attached.

it-support: Thanks. Two possible paths: (A) the device is enrolled but not yet in the Okta Device Trust allowlist, or (B) the MDM's Device Attestation didn't complete (sometimes needs a full reboot). Can you try signing in via a private browser window and paste the network request ID from Okta (if shown)?

noah: No network ID shown. I also tried rebooting and re-trying SSO, same result.

emily: @it-support FYI this is my new hire. Can we make sure Okta trusts new devices assigned by ABM?

it-support: @emily yes, our onboarding flow should auto-approve ABM-enrolled devices. @security can you check the Okta Device Trust logs for serial C02N0H3LJH (noah's device)?

security: I see an entry: device serial C02N0H3LJH, attestation status = 'user_affinity_not_set'. That means the device enrolled under userless (device affinity) or somehow skipped the token binding step. Okta requires user-affinity for Device Trust in our current policy.

noah: How do we fix 'user_affinity_not_set'?

it-support: Two fixes: 1) If the device enrolled via Automated Enrollment (DEP/ABM) but never completed the user sign-in step, we can reprovision the enrollment profile with user-affinity. 2) There's a manual workaround: install the Okta Device Trust agent profile via the enrollment URL from the welcome email while signed-in to your Redwood SSO during setup (that sets user-affinity). Can you try opening the enrollment link and installing the profile while signed into Okta?

noah: Tried the enrollment link while logged into Okta in Safari, it asked to install an 'Okta Device Trust' profile. Installed, then it asked to allow system extension in System Settings -> Privacy & Security.

it-support: That blocked extension is expected. Go to Privacy & Security and click 'Allow' for 'Okta, Inc.' then reboot. After reboot, check Okta again.

noah: I don't see an Allow button. It shows: 'System software from developer "Okta, Inc." was blocked from loading.' but no button. It only shows a note to open the General pane. Any ideas?

it-support: On macOS 14, the Allow button only appears briefly after the extension is blocked. Try: 1) Reinstall the profile and the agent (open the enrollment link again) so the block is re-triggered, then immediately open System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> General to look for the Allow button. If it still doesn't appear, run this to list extensions: 

```bash
sudo /usr/sbin/systemextensionsctl list
```

and paste output. We may need to escalate to Kernel Extension approval or use a signed system extension fallback.

noah: Ran the command. Output: "No system extensions present."

it-support: Hm, that's odd. That suggests the Okta agent uses a system extension model that didn't register. @security, could our MDM block approval of third-party system extensions by policy?

security: We do have a restriction that only approved extension bundles are whitelisted. I don't see Okta in the whitelist yet because the new onboarding whitelist job didn't include Okta last week. I'll add the Okta bundle ID to the MDM whitelist now. @it-support this will push a policy — might need Noah to reinstall the agent.

it-support: Ok pushing whitelist update to the new-hires group now. @noah after a minute try reinstalling the Okta profile from the enrollment URL and watch Privacy & Security for the Allow banner.

noah: Reinstalled and the Allow button appeared. Clicked Allow, rebooted. After reboot Okta SSO now says 'Device Trusted' and I can access Google Workspace. Woo! :tada:

it-support: Excellent. Two follow-ups: (1) we'll add the Okta bundle to the standard onboarding job so future new hires don't hit this, (2) we'll add a short step to the new-hire doc: "If SSO fails with Device Trust, reinstall Okta agent and approve system extension".

emily: Thanks team. @noah everything else OK on your side — software, VPN?

noah: VPN client (company VPN) installed fine after I allowed the extension. Only thing left is FileVault prompt didn't come up automatically during setup. Should I enable it now?

it-support: Please enable and then reply here so we can confirm escrow of the recovery key. If you prefer, we can push the escrow job from our side.

noah: Enabled FileVault, encryption started and machine restarted.

macbot: [automated] FileVault personal recovery key escrowed to KMS for device C02N0H3LJH.

it-support: Confirmed. All set. Welcome to Redwood, @noah! Ping #new-hires if anything else crops up. :)
